title: Good-truncation normalization and exact-functor compatibility
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with ordinary derived categories $D(\mathcal C),D(\mathcal D)$, localization functors $Q$, and cohomology functors $H^a$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $S_{\mathcal C}(B)=B[0]$ for the single-complex functor, and use good truncations [def-kun-truncations]. Let $\mathcal Z_{\mathcal C}$ be the full subcategory of objects $K$ with $H^a(K)=0$ for $a\ne0$; define $\mathcal Z_{\mathcal D}$ similarly.
For every representing complex $C^\bullet$ of $K\in\mathcal Z_{\mathcal C}$, let $c_C:\tau_{\le0}C\to C$ be the truncation inclusion and let $p_C:\tau_{\le0}C\to H^0(C)[0]$ have degree-zero component $\ker d_C^0\twoheadrightarrow\ker d_C^0/\operatorname{im}d_C^{-1}$ and zero components elsewhere. Both maps are quasi-isomorphisms, and, under the canonical comparison $H^0(QC)\cong H^0(C)$, the formula
$$\epsilon_{QC}=Q(p_C)\circ Q(c_C)^{-1}$$
defines a representative-independent natural isomorphism $\epsilon_K:K\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{\mathcal C}H^0(K)$ on $\mathcal Z_{\mathcal C}$. In particular, for every derived morphism $a:K\to L$ in this subcategory,
$$\epsilon_L\circ a=S_{\mathcal C}(H^0(a))\circ\epsilon_K.$$
For $K,L\in\mathcal Z_{\mathcal C}$, $a\mapsto H^0(a)$ is a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal C)}(K,L)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(H^0(K),H^0(L))$; equivalently $H^0(a)$ is the unique $b$ with $S_{\mathcal C}(b)=\epsilon_La\epsilon_K^{-1}$.
Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be additive and preserve finite limits and colimits, and let $D(F)$ be its termwise derived functor [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Let $\chi_{F,K}:FH^0(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^0(D(F)K)$ be induced by preservation of kernels, images and quotients, and let $\sigma_{F,B}:D(F)S_{\mathcal C}(B)\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{\mathcal D}(FB)$ be the termwise single-complex comparison. Then $D(F)$ sends $\mathcal Z_{\mathcal C}$ into $\mathcal Z_{\mathcal D}$ and
$$\epsilon_{D(F)K}=S_{\mathcal D}(\chi_{F,K})\circ\sigma_{F,H^0(K)}\circ D(F)(\epsilon_K),$$
$$H^0(D(F)a)\circ\chi_{F,K}=\chi_{F,L}\circ F(H^0(a)).$$
For identity functors these comparisons are identities under the canonical identification $D(\operatorname{id})\cong\operatorname{id}$; for two composable exact functors their comparisons are the composites of the individual comparisons under the canonical termwise derived-composition isomorphism. The assertions also hold in the zero abelian category.

source.place: Tag 0118, section-truncations, canonical cochain truncation at zero; Derived Categories Tag 06XS, lemma-negative-exts (2). Agent-formulated normalization and exact-functor compatibility, with inherited derivation and further localization references in report.md.

proof.text: Put $T_C=\tau_{\le0}C$ and $Z_C=\ker d_C^0$. The map $c_C$ is the identity below zero and the kernel inclusion in degree zero. Define $p_C$ by $q_C:Z_C\twoheadrightarrow H^0(C)$ in degree zero and zero in other degrees. This is a chain map: at degree $-1$ its chain equation is $q_Cd_C^{-1}=0$, because $q_C$ kills boundaries; all other equations are identities or zero equations. By [def-kun-truncations], $H^a(c_C)$ identifies the retained cohomology with $H^a(C)$ for $a\le0$ and both sides vanish for $a>0$. The target of $p_C$ has zero cohomology outside zero, as does $T_C$ under the hypothesis on $C$; in degree zero $H^0(p_C)$ is the identity of $Z_C/\operatorname{im}d_C^{-1}$. Hence both maps are quasi-isomorphisms. Localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] makes $e_C=Q(p_C)Q(c_C)^{-1}$ an isomorphism $QC\to S H^0(C)$. Both $H^0(c_C)$ and $H^0(p_C)$ are the canonical identity on that quotient, so $H^0(e_C)=1$ under $H^0(QC)\cong H^0(C)$ and $H^0(SB)\cong B$. These latter single-complex comparisons send $H^0(Sb)$ to $b$, directly from zero differentials.

source.place: Tag 0118, section-truncations, canonical cochain truncation and its cohomology; explicit cycles-to-quotient calculation at zero

proof.text: For $K\in\mathcal Z_{\mathcal C}$ choose a representative $C$ and an isomorphism $r:QC\xrightarrow{\sim}K$. Transport Step 1 to $e_K=S(H^0r)e_Cr^{-1}:K\to S H^0K$, inserting the canonical $H^0(QC)\cong H^0(C)$ comparison. Functoriality gives $H^0(e_K)=1$. Make such choices temporarily for $K,L$. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], every morphism $e_L a e_K^{-1}:S H^0K\to S H^0L$ is $S(b)$ for exactly one $b:H^0K\to H^0L$. Applying $H^0$ and the single-complex comparison from Step 1 gives $b=H^0(a)$. Conversely $b$ is attained by $e_L^{-1}S(b)e_K$. Thus $a\mapsto H^0(a)$ is bijective on these Hom sets, without yet assuming naturality of the chosen $e$'s.

source.place: Tag 06XS, lemma-negative-exts (2), full faithfulness of the degree-zero single embedding, followed by conjugation with the explicit roof

proof.text: Any two transported roofs $e_K,e'_K$ from Step 2 have the same source $K$, the same target $S H^0K$, and induce the identity on $H^0$. Both objects lie in $\mathcal Z_{\mathcal C}$, so injectivity from Step 2 gives $e_K=e'_K$. This proves independence of the complex, of $r$, and of the representatives chosen for kernels and quotients, under their canonical isomorphisms. Denote the result by $\epsilon_K$. For any $a:K\to L$, both $\epsilon_La$ and $S(H^0a)\epsilon_K$ induce $H^0a$; the same injectivity gives the displayed naturality equation. The calculation in Step 2 now gives the asserted Hom bijection and the equivalent unique-$b$ characterization for these specified $\epsilon$'s. The inverse family is natural by multiplying the naturality equation by inverses.

source.place: Tag 06XS, lemma-negative-exts (2); elementary uniqueness argument from Step 2, with Step 1 fixing the normalization

proof.text: For an exact $F$, [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] supplies $c_C^a:H^a(F C)\cong F H^a(C)$, natural in every complex and compatible with cycle inclusions and quotient projections. Invert these comparisons. The two functors $F H^a$ and $H^a D(F)$ on derived categories, pulled back along $Q$, identify with these complex-level functors by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. They invert quasi-isomorphisms. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] (2) to descend $(c_C^a)^{-1}$ to a natural isomorphism $\chi^a_{F,K}:F H^a(K)\to H^a(D(F)K)$. At $a=0$ this is exactly the stipulated kernel/image/quotient comparison $\chi_{F,K}$, and its naturality is $H^0(D(F)a)\chi_{F,K}=\chi_{F,L}F(H^0a)$ for every derived morphism. For $a\ne0$ and $K\in\mathcal Z_{\mathcal C}$ its source is zero, since $F$ preserves the zero object. Thus $D(F)K\in\mathcal Z_{\mathcal D}$. No boundedness or injective-resolution hypothesis is used.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; homology.tex Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor; categories.tex Tag 04VG and the natural-transformation localization enhancement stated in the cited node

proof.text:
Construct $t_C:F(T_C)\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{F C}$ termwise: it is the identity comparison below zero, the preserved-kernel comparison $F Z_C\cong\ker F(d_C^0)$ in degree zero, and the canonical zero-object comparison above zero. These are isomorphisms by [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology] (a). The kernel universal property checks the chain equation at $-1$; elsewhere it is immediate. Let $s_B:F(B[0])\cong(FB)[0]$ be the termwise single-complex comparison. The first chain-map equation is $c_{F C}t_C=F(c_C)$. The second says that $p_{F C}t_C$ is the composite $F(T_C)\xrightarrow{F(p_C)}F(H^0C[0])\xrightarrow{s_{H^0C}}(FH^0C)[0]\xrightarrow{(\chi^0_{F,QC})[0]}H^0(F C)[0]$, using the factorization comparisons. At degree zero this is precisely $q_{F C}t_C^0=\chi^0_{F,QC}F(q_C)$, the projection compatibility in [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]; all other components vanish. Localize these two equations, replace $Q(c_{F C})^{-1}$ by $Q(t_C)Q(Fc_C)^{-1}$, and cancel $Q(t_C)$. Termwise derived factorization [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] gives
$$\epsilon_{D(F)QC}=S_{\mathcal D}(\chi_{F,QC})\,\sigma_{F,H^0(QC)}\,D(F)(\epsilon_{QC}).$$

source.place: Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor, preserved kernels and cokernels; Tag 0118, section-truncations; explicit two chain-map equations and their localization

proof.text: The comparison $\sigma_{F,B}$ is natural in $B$: termwise, a map $b:B\to B'$ gives the same degree-zero map $F(b)$ around both sides of its square and zero maps elsewhere; apply the natural factorization [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Step 4 makes $\chi$ natural on all derived morphisms, and Step 3 makes $\epsilon$ natural. Thus both sides of the equality in Step 5 are natural in $K\in\mathcal Z_{\mathcal C}$. For any representative isomorphism $r:QC\to K$, naturality says that each side at $K$, precomposed with $D(F)r$, equals $S(H^0(D(F)r))$ followed after that side at $QC$. Step 5 identifies the latter sides; cancel the isomorphism $D(F)r$. This proves the required exact-functor compatibility for every $K$.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; naturality and isomorphism cancellation using Steps 3--5

proof.text: For $F=\operatorname{id}$, the preserved-kernel comparison is the identity by uniqueness of a factorization through the kernel inclusion, and the quotient comparison is the identity by uniqueness after the epimorphism $Z_C\twoheadrightarrow H^aC$. The termwise single comparison is also the identity. Hence $\chi$ and $\sigma$ are identities under $D(\operatorname{id})\cong\operatorname{id}$. For composable exact functors $F,G$, the composite $G F Z_C\to G Z_{FC}\to Z_{GFC}$ and the direct preserved-kernel comparison have the same composite with the kernel inclusion; that inclusion is monic, so they agree. The image and quotient comparisons agree by the corresponding mono and epi cancellations [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology]. Consequently, at complexes, $\chi_{GF,C}=\chi_{G,FC}\,G(\chi_{F,C})$, and $s_{GF,B}=s_{G,FB}\,G(s_{F,B})$ termwise. The equality $C(GF)=C(G)C(F)$ gives the canonical derived-composition isomorphism by localization uniqueness [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] (1),(2). Its part (3) descends these equalities to $\chi_{GF,K}=\chi_{G,D(F)K}G(\chi_{F,K})$ and $\sigma_{GF,B}=\sigma_{G,FB}D(G)(\sigma_{F,B})$ under that isomorphism. Substitution into Step 6 gives exactly the composite compatibility for $\epsilon$ as well.

source.place: Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor; categories.tex Tag 04VG with the natural-transformation enhancement; uniqueness of kernel/image/quotient comparisons and localized comparisons

proof.text: In the zero abelian category every object is zero and every Hom set is a singleton. All displayed maps, their inverses, and their comparisons are its unique maps. The kernel, quotient, and Hom-bijection calculations above still apply, including $\operatorname{Hom}(0,0)$, so this case requires no nonzero-object assumption.
